probe: M12 part c.2: probe 5 (m7-probe5-derive-proxy-gpu.json) repeated in Safari: can the profiler hand WebKit a derived pass descriptor that carries timestampWrites?
head: a4708c8
machine: Apple M2 Pro / Metal, Safari 27.0.1 (macOS 27.0.1, 26A434), safaridriver 27.0.1 (W3C WebDriver execute/async), page http://localhost:5173/?mode=B
method: The Chrome script of probe 5 was not committed; this one is rebuilt from the method recorded in m7-probe5-derive-proxy-gpu.json. One fresh device with timestamp-query. Per derivation set: one query set (2 stamps per case), one command encoder; each case opens ONE pass through the derived descriptor and draws a full-screen triangle into a 512x512 rgba8unorm target (render) or dispatches 64 workgroups of 64 (compute); then resolveQuerySet + copy in the same command buffer, readback. A validation + internal error scope wraps the encoding and the submit of each set. Three sets over the same six cases: run2 (the Proxy of the Chrome JSON, verbatim), engineDerive (FrameRecorder.derive imported from /src/render/timestamp-intercept.ts: the code the profiler ships), objectCreateControl (run1 viaCreate). The script is in `script`.

run2.derivation: const source = desc ?? {}; new Proxy({}, { get: (_target, key) => (key === 'timestampWrites' ? tw : Reflect.get(source, key, source)) }) — verbatim from m7-probe5-derive-proxy-gpu.json run2

engineDerive.derivation: FrameRecorder.derive() of ts/src/render/timestamp-intercept.ts (the code the profiler runs), imported from the dev server

objectCreateControl.derivation: Object.create(desc ?? {}, { timestampWrites: { value: tw, enumerable: true } }) — run1 viaCreate, the control

results.0 render class #private: THROWS TypeError: Cannot access invalid private field (evaluating 'this.#view')

verdict.run2: 6/6 ok, no validation or internal error, the frozen original unchanged, no original written
verdict.objectCreateControl: case 0 (class with a #private getter) THROWS TypeError: Cannot access invalid private field (evaluating 'this.#view') — the Object.create failure Chrome showed (C8); the other 5 ok
verdict.reading: WebKit reads a pass descriptor with [[Get]] only, like Chrome: a Proxy over a fresh empty object that reads every member from the original, with the original as receiver, is accepted for render and compute passes, from a class with a #private getter, a frozen literal with an own timestampWrites: undefined, a literal with a this-getter, and undefined, null and {label} compute descriptors. The spec's §8.2 fallback ({ ...desc, timestampWrites }) is not needed in Safari.

stampAnomalies.what: in the first run, engineDerive pair 5 (the compute case 5, with work) carries exactly run2 pair 5's stamps, and objectCreateControl pair 0 (whose pass threw and never opened) exactly engineDerive pair 0's. Classified with two repeats (same six cases and derivations; every stamp compared with every stamp read before):

repeatBothResolveModes.setup: 6 iterations, set order rotated each iteration; each set once with the resolve in the same command buffer as the passes ('same-cb', what the profiler does) and once in a second submit after device.queue.onSubmittedWorkDone() ('after-done')

repeatRenderLast.setup: 12 iterations, same-cb only, run2 and engineDerive, cases reordered so the three render passes come LAST (compute 3,4,5 then render 0,1,2)

reading: A pass that opened and did work gets fresh stamps, except the LAST compute pass of the command buffer when the resolve is in that same command buffer: 6 of 18 same-cb sets in the first repeat, 6 of 24 with three render passes after it; never a render pass, never an earlier compute pass, and never with the resolve in a later submit (0 of 102 passes). Its pair then reads what the query set held before, so resolveQuerySet does not wait for that pass's samples.

A never-written pair of a NEW query set resolves to the stamps of a query set destroyed before (12 of 12), not 0: WebKit reuses the storage of a destroyed query set without clearing it. Chrome gives 0 on a fresh query set (M7 probe 2).
The derivation plays no part: the stale pairs fall in every set, the engine's derive included.

liveProfiler.what: does the race reach the engine? The profiler resolves in the same command buffer, and in its graph cull (or the last sort pass) is the last compute pass; a raced pair would equal the last value read at its index, so the profiler would discard the frame as 'stale' (timestamp-frames.ts StampHistory), not mis-measure it

oneQuadBench10s.scene: ?mode=B&bench, one 2D quad at the origin, camera (0,0,0) zoom 1: little GPU work between cull and the resolve

liveProfiler.reading: 0 discards of any kind over 1200 + 600 live frames: the race stays in the synthetic probe

repeatScriptNote: the repeats are the same script with the per-set body in a loop over iterations and resolve modes, staleness = a stamp value already read before: m12-probe5-repeat-safari.js (repeatBothResolveModes) and m12-probe5-renderlast-safari.js (repeatRenderLast), committed from the session scratchpad in the M12 fix round
